state: Watched the Novaris Corp launch event live. Underwhelming specs for the price tag, hard pass on chasing this one. Trimmed my position after the keynote. $NOVA
Halodyne Robotics ($HALO) price target moved to $58 from $52 after this morning's note, while a separate desk trimmed theirs to $45. Two very different views on the same quarter.
Wow, another 'in-line' quarter from Tidewell Logistics, be still my heart 🙄. Not adding here, might lighten up if guidance stays this flat next time. $TIDE
Qubitrix ($QBIT) smashes estimates: revenue up 210% YoY, raises full-year guidance by 40%, and announces an accelerated buyback. Shares halted for volatility after opening up 35% pre-market.
$EMBT: Line 3 at the plant is down for unscheduled maintenance per this morning's 8-K filing. Management says no change to Q3 output guidance at this time. Filing linked in our bio.

Everyone's panicking over the downgrade on Vynetic Health, sure, the stock is definitely doomed forever 🙄. New to this but I just put half my paycheck into more shares, this looks like the buy of the decade to me. $VYNE

First time buying individual stocks and Gravitas Motors just posted numbers that made my jaw drop, deliveries doubled and they're finally profitable. Put in another order this morning, going all-in on this one. $GRVT

Ok so apparently Nimbaly Cloud got hit with a class action over last month's outage lol. No idea if this actually moves the stock or if it's one of those nothingburger filings, anyone know more? $NMBL
Regulatory panel green-lit the Merlinox Pharma trial extension. Grabbed a few July calls, small size, not betting the house but couldn't resist. $MRLN 👀
Judge just tossed the bulk of the lawsuit against Orbital Foods. Not a moonshot catalyst but I like the setup enough to add a few September calls. $ORBT
Streamcore Networks just locked in a multi-year deal with one of the big telecom carriers. Added a small starter position this morning, want to see the next print before going bigger. $STRM

Massive line at Voltaic Batteries' overflow plant this morning after a competitor's fire took out half the region's supply, orders are getting rerouted here fast. Sized up huge premarket, this gaps and holds. $VLTA 🔥
Zephyrion Air reported earnings this morning, revenue and EPS both came in right at consensus. Not doing anything with my shares either way. $ZPHR

Goldenreef Mining announced a $200M buyback today, cool cool, except they had to raise debt to do it while the CFO just dumped half his shares. Dumped my whole position, this is circling the drain. $GLDN
Wanderlux Travel authorizes a new $50M buyback program, its first since 2019. Shares ticked up 3% in early trading as a few desks called it a sign of management confidence. $WNDR

Not sure what to make of the Axiom Robotics tie-up with that retail chain, could be a huge new revenue stream or just a pilot program that goes nowhere. Holding what I have, not adding or trimming until there's more detail. $AXRB

1/ Two more research notes out on Halcyon Steelworks this week, one raised to buy, one cut to hold. Read through both this weekend. $HLCY
2/ The bull case leans on cost cuts from the new furnace line, the bear case worries the contract wins were one-time. Both fair points honestly.
3/ Not changing my position size either way, this was already a small piece of the portfolio and I'm just watching how the next two quarters play out.
Forsythe Retail's big partnership with that delivery app just fell apart, deal is dead. Sold my entire position at the open, this stock is finished. $FRST
Kernelytics announced a new buyback today. Not thrilled they're doing this instead of paying down debt, trimmed a small piece of my position on the news. $KRNL

Oh no, the chart 'looks terrible' according to twitter, whatever will I do 🙄. Bought another full position this week, I think Pixelforge Media triples from here regardless of what the squiggly lines say. $PXLF
New to investing but the lawsuit headlines around Solectra Power have me nervous. Sold about a quarter of my shares today just to be safe, might sell more if it drags on. $SLTC

1/ Chart update on Meridian Kinetics: shares are consolidating between $34 support and $38 resistance for the third straight week. $MDKN
2/ Volume has been below the 20-day average on both tests of support, no clear breakout signal yet in either direction.
3/ Will post again if we get a close outside the range on above-average volume. No position currently.
Halberd Motors halts all Class-4 production pending an NHTSA-style review; shares limit-down at the open, volume already 5x the 30-day average and options pricing in a 40% implied move. $HLBD
Even I'll admit the reaction to Vantage Foods' recall looks overdone. Added a starter position on the pullback, first buy from me in over a year. $VTGF

1/ Been sitting on this Thornfield Systems lawsuit overhang for two years now. $THRN
2/ Settlement filed today, structured payout over 8 quarters, no admission of wrongdoing, cash reserves comfortably cover it.
3/ Added a bit more to the position this week now that the tail risk is off the table, still a small weight in the portfolio overall.
Regulators just rejected Halyard Biotech's application outright, no path to appeal until next cycle. Rolled everything into December puts this morning, this one's headed to zero territory imo. $HYRD
Solenne Robotics board just tripled the buyback authorization. YOLOing my whole account into January calls, strikes way out of the money, this is my Tesla-in-2013 moment. 🚀 $SLNR

Board tapped the former COO of a much larger rival to take over as CEO of Palisade Freight starting next quarter. We're nudging our rating up a notch, execution risk still keeps us from going further out on the limb. $PLSF

Update: the exclusive supply deal between Cascade Robotics and its largest customer has been terminated effective immediately, the customer confirms it is moving 100% of orders to a competitor starting next month. $CSCR
Oh great, another wave of 0DTE calls flooding into Ferrow Tech into the print, what could go wrong 🙄. Added a few puts here, wouldn't chase this pop. $FRRW

First leadership change I've been through as a shareholder, wasn't expecting the CFO to also hand in notice the same week as the new CEO news. Trimmed a small chunk of my Larkspur Media position while I wait for the next call. $LRKM
Earnings from Bramblewood Foods came in a bit light on margins. Picked up a few near-dated puts, nothing huge, just a small hedge against more downside. $BWFD
Third downgrade this week on Ridgeline Apparel, target slashed to $4 from $19. Loaded September puts, deep ITM, see you at zero. $RDGL

1/ Trying to understand this Brightfield Energy buyback announcement before I do anything with my small position. $BRFE
2/ From what I can tell it's a modest $30M program, not huge relative to their market cap, and they didn't say much about timing.
3/ Not sure yet if this is a meaningful signal or just routine capital allocation, going to wait for the next earnings call before deciding anything.

Solmark Industries names the founder of a prior 10-bagger startup as new CEO effective immediately. A couple of analysts flag near-term transition costs, but shares are up 28% on the news with call option volume hitting an all-time high. $SLMK

1/ THEY DID IT. Board just named the guy who turned around two other companies as the new CEO of Cobalt Ridge Mining. $CBRM
2/ This dude has a 15 year track record of doubling revenue within 18 months of taking over, not even joking, look him up.
3/ Went and bought as many shares as my account would let me this morning, not selling a single share until this thing is a completely different company.
Tavistock Semiconductors just broke out above 18-month resistance on volume 6x the daily average, and three separate desks raised price targets by more than 50% within the hour. $TVSC
'Isolated incident,' they said, about the third 'isolated incident' at the Ashgrove Materials plant this year 🙄. Not blowing up my position over it, just took a little off the top. $ASHG

1/ Confused why Driftwood Telecom would announce a buyback the same week they suspended the dividend. $DRFT
2/ Read a few threads saying companies do this to prop up the stock price when the underlying business is in real trouble.
3/ Decided this is too risky for me, sold my entire position today, don't want to find out the hard way.
Wrenfield Data unveils its new platform lineup at the trade show today. Not planning to do anything with my position until we see actual usage numbers next quarter. $WRNF

Copperlyne Mining pulled back the curtain on its new extraction platform this morning, and it's a bigger step-change than the sell-side was modeling. We're raising numbers across the board and see meaningfully more room to run than our prior target implied. $CPRL

1/ Kestrel Dynamics' backup facility just came online three weeks ahead of schedule after the main plant hiccup last month. $KSTR
2/ Turns out the redundancy plan they built two years ago is actually working, output guidance unchanged and now they've got extra capacity nobody priced in.
3/ Went in heavy premarket, this is a top position for me now, I think the market is way behind on how good this redundancy story actually is.

1/ Marrow Biotech announced a buyback today and I wanted to like it but something feels off. $MRWB
2/ They're doing this the same quarter cash from operations dropped for the first time since I've owned the stock.
3/ Sold off a small piece just to lower my exposure a bit while I figure out if this is actually a good sign or not.
Anchorpoint Financial's print beat on both lines and management raised the low end of full-year guidance. We're bumping our price target up and staying constructive into the next quarter. $ANCP
Petrel Shipping: put/call ratio sitting right at its 6-month average, implied vol barely above realized. Maintaining our current rating and estimates unchanged heading into the print. $PTRL

1/ Lodestar Mining just broke below the 200-day for the first time in two years. $LDST
2/ Lower highs for six straight weeks now, volume picking up on every down day and drying up on the bounces.
3/ Rolled everything into puts this morning, this chart is broken and I don't want to be anywhere near it on the way down.

1/ Oh sure, call the quarter 'disappointing' because revenue only grew 18% instead of 20%, very rational market reaction this morning. $BRKN
2/ Strip out the one-time freight charges buried in COGS and margins actually expanded year over year.
3/ We're using the overreaction to nudge our rating up a notch, this looks like a buyable dip rather than the start of a real slide.

Even I have to admit the put wall on Wintermere Media getting torn through like this isn't normal, dealers are scrambling to hedge and this could easily gap another 20% before it's over. Bought my first calls on this name ever. $WNTM

Options desk note: put volume in $SLCR is running about 3x its 20-day average this morning, concentrated in near-dated strikes below the market. Flow like this usually precedes a soft print. We'd trim into any bounce here.
Options flow alert: call volume in $KVNA is running roughly 3x the 30-day average this morning, concentrated in strikes $5 above the current price expiring next month, according to trading desk data.

Still learning charts but $FNDL just closed below its 50-day for the third day in a row and couldn't reclaim it on the bounce attempt. Not loving what I'm seeing, might just wait this one out for now.

$HLXA's CEO is 'stepping down to pursue other opportunities,' three weeks after the CFO left and two board members resigned. Sure, nothing to see here. This leadership team is falling apart in real time.
Good news on $BZLR: the recall is only about 3,000 units, way smaller than the rumors floating around yesterday. Stock's actually green premarket on the relief. Adding a little here.
Ok the $BRSK labeling violation thing is apparently a real fine now, not just a rumor. Regulators still call it minor but it's another headline nobody needed this month. Holding but watching close.

1/ Redwing Analytics just got upgraded to Buy from Hold this morning. $RDWG
2/ Funny thing is the new price target is basically where it's already trading, like a 4% bump from here, not some crazy call.
3/ Still counting it as a win though, first upgrade this stock's had all year and the desk finally admits the growth numbers are real. Adding some here.

1/ Raising our rating on Quantek Systems to Overweight from Neutral this morning. $QNTK
2/ Recent enterprise contract wins point to durable double-digit revenue growth into next year, ahead of where our model had it.
3/ New price target implies modest upside from current levels; not calling for a re-rating yet, but the setup here has clearly improved.

Watching the news out of $MTRX's main plant with a knot in my stomach. Three-alarm fire, production offline indefinitely, and early reports say the core assembly line is a total loss. Trimmed most of my position this morning, this changes the thesis.
$GRPK getting hit with an environmental lawsuit from the state today, stock's down but not falling off a cliff. Took some profit off the table into the dip, not fully out though.

$DKWD got named in a supplier dispute lawsuit today, stock barely moved on the headline. Legal desk says this kind of contract claim gets settled or tossed within a quarter most of the time. Not touching my position either way.

$TRDX's smelter line 2 is down for a few days after an equipment fault, output guidance trimmed slightly for the quarter. Sold a chunk of my position into the news, small hit but not sticking around to find out how small.

So $ARKD's big game launch is trending for all the wrong reasons, servers down for six hours and refund requests already flooding every forum. This was supposed to be the whole thesis. Closed out my position, can't defend this one.
BREAKING: $IRVL signs exclusive multi-year supply agreement with the Continental Defense Alliance, deal valued at $2.1B. Shares halted for volatility premarket.

$BRLP's new panel line sold through its entire first production run in under four hours, site crashed twice from demand. Backorders already stretching into next quarter. Loaded up more this morning, this is a different stock now.
Options volume in $FERV ticked up a bit today but nothing unusual, strikes spread evenly on both sides of the current price. Nothing here that changes my long-term view either way, just noise.

Sold my $RVLN calls straight into the partnership pop this morning, chart's been rolling over for weeks and this rally has the feel of one last squeeze before the drop. Puts back on the board once the crush settles.
$HLBS earnings were rough, missed on both revenue and EPS, and they slashed full-year guidance by almost a third. Sold basically everything this morning, don't want to catch this falling knife.
$BLTF's CEO is stepping down 'for health reasons' effective next month, no successor named yet. Stock dipped on the uncertainty, trimmed a bit while we wait for more clarity, not bailing completely.
$NGRT dropped the new flagship concept store today. 👀 not touching this one either way, just here for the popcorn 🍿
Rolled some of my $FRNG April calls into puts after the batch recall headline hit. Doesn't feel like a one-day dip to me, might drag on the desk for a bit before it clears up.
$CPRH drops a fresh buyback authorization and the tape actually cooperates for once. Wasn't planning on it, but added shares back this morning, riding this one for now.
$VEXS board approves a $150M share buyback program, to be executed over the next 18 months, the company confirmed in a filing this morning.

1/ Not the update anyone wanted from $AURS this morning, fire at the main fab overnight.
2/ Early word from the fire department is the clean room and most of the equipment inside is a total loss, rebuild timeline unknown.
3/ Dumped my whole position at the open, this was basically their only fab and I don't want to hold through however long a rebuild takes.

1/ Called this one. $CARW is expanding its recall to a third state after more contamination reports came in overnight.
2/ Two hospitalizations now linked to the batch, and the company still hasn't said how far back this goes in their supply chain.
3/ Anyone still holding this waiting for a bounce is going to be waiting a long time. Sitting this all the way out.
$SGWV's new device launch is off to a solid start, pre-orders running ahead of what the desk expected. Added a starter position into the move, liking the early reaction here.
Small equipment fire at $CBRD's site this morning, contained within twenty minutes, no injuries and no impact to production guidance. Basically a non-event, not touching my position over this.

$VLLM finally cleared the resistance it's been chopping under for six weeks, closed above it on real volume too. Picked up some short-dated calls into the close, first clean setup this name's had in a while.

$OMVX reports its new wearable health monitor saw stronger-than-expected initial demand in its first week, with retail partners requesting additional inventory ahead of schedule, the company said Tuesday.
$CASC beat estimates on both lines this morning, nothing blowout but a clean beat-and-raise. Added a bit into the move, liking the steady improvement here quarter over quarter.
$PXTN's just been chopping sideways in the same $3 range for a month now, no real breakout or breakdown either direction. Kind of boring honestly, not doing anything with my shares right now.
$LRKS just got FULL FDA approval, not just the fast-track designation everyone expected. YOLOing into weekly calls right now, this is a completely different company starting Monday. 🚀

Nothing to worry about at all, just the heaviest put buying we've seen in $NMBS all year, concentrated three strikes below the market into next week's print. Totally routine positioning, I'm sure. Moving to Sell here.

Moving $ASHC to Sell after this morning's filing: a class action alleging the company misstated reserves for two straight years. If even half of this holds up, the balance sheet implications are severe. Cutting our price target sharply.

1/ Quick note on the $VSTR recall announced this morning, about 40,000 units for a steering sensor fix.
2/ Cost estimate from the company is modest, low double-digit millions, and the fix itself is a quick dealer visit, not a full teardown.
3/ Trimming our estimates slightly for the quarter to reflect the charge and some brand friction, nudging our rating down to Hold from Buy.
$LNTR has indefinitely postponed the launch of its new diagnostic device after internal testing turned up safety failures, the company confirmed Wednesday, without giving a revised timeline.
$FBRG renewed its processing partnership with a mid-size retailer today, nothing new really, just an extension of an existing deal. IV barely moved on the headline, no real edge here either way.

Rival toy maker just pulled its entire holiday lineup off shelves over a safety recall, and every retailer I follow is scrambling to fill the gap with $WNHL product instead. Loaded up hard this morning, this timing could not be better for them.

Even I have to admit this is a big deal: $MRLC just hired the exec who tripled Fernwood Capital's stock in four years as their new CEO. I've been negative on this name for a year and I'm actually buying on this one.

Didn't expect to say this about $DRPL, but the new distribution partnership they signed actually looks decent, real shelf space in over 2,000 new stores. Not turning into a bull on this name, but I nudged my short down a bit.

Good news for once with $PTCE, the pipeline expansion permit got approved today. Still learning how much this actually matters long-term but it seems like a positive step, added a small amount to my position.

Following the outage at a competitor's fab this week, we expect some near-term order flow to shift toward $WVFT's spare capacity. Nudging our estimates up modestly and moving our rating to Overweight from Neutral.
Was hyped for the $CRSL partnership announcement all week and it turned out to be a tiny regional licensing deal. Kind of a letdown honestly, trimmed some of my position after that headline. 📉

$VNTX says it's fully insured against the supplier lawsuit and doesn't expect any operational disruption. Fair enough, but legal overhangs like this tend to cap a stock for a while regardless, so I'm not adding more here even though I'm staying put.

Looking at the $FLXG chart and honestly I can't tell if this is a base forming or just drifting sideways before another leg down. Going to sit on my hands until something clearer shows up, no idea which way this breaks.
$PLMO's routine compliance audit came back clean today, exactly what everyone expected going in. Stock didn't even blink on the headline. Moving on, nothing to do here.
$GLMR just announced a $500M buyback ON TOP of a special dividend?! 🚀🚀 LOADING UP HERE, this thing is about to absolutely RIP 🔥
Wait... 🟢🟢🟢 $NRLX just got the green light?? Locking in shares right now, every alert on my phone is going off at once 😳🚀
$DYNM just ripped through its all-time high on 5x average volume, clean breakout, no resistance left above. To the moon from here, absolutely loaded up. 🚀🚀🚀
$CLPT just printed a death cross on the daily, broke the last support that mattered, and didn't even get a dead cat bounce on the retest. Zero reason to catch this one. 📉
Oh no, a $SLRK shareholder is suing because the annual meeting started four minutes late. Truly an existential threat to the business here. 🙄 Anyway, nothing about this changes the thesis either way.

1/ Update on the $THRF recall scare from last month: turns out it was way overblown.
2/ The safety agency finished its full review and found zero injuries linked to the batch in question, clearing it completely.
3/ Stock's already ripping on the news and I'm honestly relieved I didn't panic-sell like I almost did. Added more shares this morning instead.
seeing way more put volume than usual stacking up on $FRST near the 20 strike this week, kinda spooked ngl. still holding my shares but trimmed the weeklies
$CNDP broke below the 50-day this morning which is ugly, but reclaimed it by lunch and closed at the highs of the day on 2x average volume. watching for a breakout over $34 next
Oh no, 15 units recalled out of 2.3 million shipped, $KSTA is doomed 🙄 guess I'll go ahead and load more shares at this discount then, thoughts and prayers to the shorts
What amazing timing, $PLSD CEO 'stepping down to spend more time with family' the exact week auditors showed up unannounced. Sure, nothing weird there. Selling into every bounce from here 🙄

1/ $WLBK got a target trim this morning, nothing dramatic, just a few analysts nudging numbers down after the guidance reset last month.
2/ Nothing new to me, I said the multiple was stretched back in spring. This just confirms the group is finally catching up to reality.
3/ Not adding here, just watching the cuts continue to trickle in over the next few weeks.
Oh wow, huge shocking regulatory news for $IRNC today... they renewed the same license they've renewed every three years since 1994 🙄 truly can't believe the alerts blew up my phone for this
Rarely say this but $NMBS locking in a multi-year supply deal with three of the largest cloud operators changes my whole thesis here. Closing out the short today.

1/ ok the $OBSN partnership deal with Meridian Data Centers has some messy terms, revenue share is lower than I hoped ngl
2/ BUT the volume commitment guarantee is insane, 400k units a year minimum for 5 years, that alone justifies way more than the current market cap
3/ adding aggressively into any weakness tomorrow, this is a company-changing deal even with the so-so margins 🚀
Seeing decent volume on both calls and puts for $BLUW ahead of earnings next week, honestly can't tell which way the smart money is leaning so I'm staying flat for now.
BREAKING: $RDWD Q3 revenue comes in 22% below consensus, guidance for the next two quarters pulled entirely citing 'demand uncertainty.' Shares halted for volatility.
$VRTA bringing in the ex-Nimbus Cloud ops chief as CEO starting next month, market barely reacting yet but I like the resume enough to add some March calls
$HLCY just authorized a buyback worth nearly a third of the current float, the largest in company history by a wide margin. Increasing my position size meaningfully this week.
$AMBL announcing a buyback... funded by taking on more debt while insiders keep selling into it lol. feels like a signal not a strength tbh, lightened up today
Upgrading $LUMH to Overweight, raising our price target to $58 from $50 on improving margin trends. Modest upside from here but risk/reward has turned favorable.
$FNWK renewed its standard annual buyback authorization at the same size as last year, no change to the pace of repurchases. Business as usual.
$SLST just blew past estimates on every single line, revenue up 41% YoY and raised full year guidance twice in one call. Stock ripping premarket, adding on any dip today 🚀
Noticing a decent stack of call buying on $CRLR for the March 45s, more than the usual flow for this name. Grabbed a small starter position to ride along.
$TTND CEO forced out immediately after the board found accounting irregularities dating back two years. Puts printing, dumped my shares at the open.
$MRLW confirming their previously announced succession plan, current COO taking over as CEO January 1st exactly as outlined at last year's investor day. No surprises.
Our initial read on $FRST's new console launch is a bit underwhelming, pre-order figures tracking below the prior generation's pace. We see modest downside risk to near-term revenue estimates.

so the FDA just approved $AURP's lead drug for full marketing authorization, ahead of the review deadline too. new to investing but even I know this is huge, put in a bigger order than I usually would

1/ $PNGV CEO announced retirement effective end of year, board says search for successor already underway internally and externally
2/ stock barely moved on the news, desk chatter is pretty split between people who think it's overdue and people who think current leadership gets an unfair rap
3/ not touching this either way until there's an actual name attached to the role

1/ $STRL new CEO used to run ops at a much bigger airline so that's a plus on paper, but he's never actually been the top guy anywhere before
2/ some of the old management team is staying, some key names already jumped ship this week, kind of a wash honestly
3/ not sure this changes anything meaningful for the stock either direction, holding what I have and watching the next earnings call for signal
$CBLT technical picture continues to deteriorate, now trading below both the 50 and 200-day moving averages with declining volume on recent bounces. We'd wait for a base to form before stepping in.
$NRDT just suspended its entire buyback program to 'preserve liquidity,' which is corporate speak for the balance sheet being in worse shape than they've let on. Shorting more here.
$WLBK issuing a voluntary recall on one batch of its oat milk line due to a labeling error, company says less than 0.1% of shipped units affected and no health risk identified.

one shop bumped their $QNTX target by a couple bucks today but three others slashed theirs by double digits and pulled their buy ratings entirely, average target now sits below where we're trading. closing out the rest of my position

regulators cleared $IRNC's new policy product for sale but tacked on extra capital reserve requirements that eat into the margin story a bit. trimmed a few shares, still holding the core position though

$BRPT announced a 'strategic partnership' with a regional tutoring chain, no dollar figures disclosed and the other side has like 40 locations total. Was hoping for something bigger, sold half my shares on the news.
$SLRA just got double-upgraded from Underweight straight to Buy, with the price target nearly tripled to $90. Adding a full new position first thing tomorrow.
$CSCB recalling a small batch of seasonal cans over a labeling mix-up, standard stuff, company expects it to be resolved within the week with no material cost impact.

1/ new to reading charts but even I can see $TTND just broke below every major moving average on the heaviest volume day in over a year
2/ support levels that held for the last three pullbacks all gave way today without even a bounce attempt
3/ got scared and sold everything at the close, don't want to catch this falling knife while I'm still learning

1/ $MRLW CFO stepping up to interim CEO after the sudden departure announced this morning, no reason given beyond 'personal reasons'
2/ market doesn't love the lack of a real explanation, and an internal placeholder pick usually means a longer search process ahead
3/ closed out my calls, might revisit once there's more clarity on who actually takes the permanent seat

1/ Thrilled to see $VRTA announce yet another 'transformative partnership,' the fourth one this year with a company nobody has heard of and no financial terms attached.
2/ I'm sure this one will finally move the needle, just like the last three totally did, truly a banner year for meaningful, revenue-generating tie-ups.
3/ Cutting our estimates and moving to Sell, we've heard this story enough times to stop pretending it means anything.

small equipment fire at one of $FRRT's plants got contained in under 20 minutes with zero injuries and insurance covering the full repair cost, production barely skipped a beat. bought the dip on the initial headline scare

regulators technically approved $AURP's drug but slapped a black box warning on it and required a costly post-market study, the kind of approval that reads like a rejection in disguise. adding to my short here
$CBLT just got their mining permit renewal denied outright by regulators, forcing an immediate halt to operations at their primary site. Puts printing hard today, in for size.
oh no the lawsuit against $KSTA got thrown out with prejudice and they don't even have to pay a cent, guess the bears were right all along 🙄 loading more shares on the open tomorrow

1/ Regulators approved $OBSN's spectrum license renewal but attached new pricing caps on a portion of their enterprise contracts starting next year
2/ We estimate this shaves roughly 2-3% off our prior EBITDA forecast for FY next year, a modest but real headwind
3/ Trimming our price target slightly to reflect the narrower margin outlook, maintaining our existing rating

1/ one of the bigger shops moved $AMBL from Buy to Hold this morning, target barely trimmed but the rating change itself is what's got people talking
2/ nothing in the note really changes the long term story, just softer near term demand they're flagging
3/ not selling but definitely not adding more until this settles down, watching from the sidelines for now

1/ omg $CNDP recalling literally 40 controllers out of 2 million shipped because of a loose screw, the sky is absolutely falling 🙄
2/ seeing people in the replies acting like this is a bankruptcy event over a screw, kind of wild honestly
3/ not selling, not buying more either, this changes basically nothing about the thesis either way

1/ $VKTR just recalled its entire flagship product line, all 3.2 million units, after multiple reports of battery fires causing injuries. Production halted indefinitely pending investigation.
2/ Been flagging the supply chain corners they've been cutting for over a year now and nobody wanted to hear it. This is looking like an extinction-level event for the balance sheet.
3/ Class action lawyers already circling and major retailers are pulling remaining inventory from shelves nationwide. Closed my eyes and shorted more into the open today.

1/ $GRVX had a small fire at their Ohio plant this morning, contained within the hour and no injuries reported, but that site does run about 15% of total output.
2/ Company says full production resumes by Friday and insurance covers the equipment damage, so I'm not seeing much read-through to the numbers either way.
3/ Grabbed a few contracts each direction today honestly, don't have enough to lean hard one way yet, waiting on the official statement tomorrow before doing anything bigger.

1/ $HMBX just reported and it's an absolute disaster, revenue missed by 30%, guidance cut for the third straight quarter, and they're suspending the dividend entirely 💀
2/ Management basically admitted on the call they have no idea when this turns around, CFO couldn't even answer basic analyst questions without stumbling.
3/ This isn't a dip to buy, this thing is heading toward zero territory. Dumping everything I have left first thing tomorrow.

$TRQX just landed a supply deal with Meridian Retail for a 'modest' 150 stores to start... yeah because store count is definitely the only thing that matters here 🙄 still a decent incremental win, added a small starter position today.

$NXLB just picked up every order Bridgeline Foods can't fill now that their plant is down for the rest of the quarter. Phones ringing nonstop over here, can't keep enough on shelves. Backing up the truck at the open tomorrow 🚚💰

$PLYN launched their new subscription tier today and the pricing and features matched exactly what they'd previewed last quarter. Not sure this moves the needle much either way, holding what I have and watching for early reviews before doing anything.

$SLVK settled the patent suit for $8M, a fraction of the $200M originally sought, though the settlement terms do set a precedent the same plaintiffs' firm could use elsewhere. Overhang's mostly lifted here, nibbled a bit more today.
$MPLR reclaimed its 50-day moving average this week on above-average volume, first time since spring. Not exactly a moonshot setup but the trend is quietly improving, added a bit more to my position.

bro $DRFT's main plant has been sitting completely dark for like 4 days now after whatever happened there, and nobody on the ground has heard a peep from management since it started. pulled everything I had this morning, not sticking around to find out what it was
